newsitem.title: USA: CSCE coffee ends higher as bull run continues.
newsitem.headline: CSCE coffee ends higher as bull run continues.

text.p: CSCE coffee prices edged higher on Friday, led by a sharp advance in the spot contract, amid persistent concerns about near-term supplies, trading sources said.

Benchmark December futures shot up 2.35 cents per lb Friday, to 109.80 cents, the highest close in four weeks. The contract briefly pierced crucial psychological resistance at 110 cents, rising to a high of 110.20 before settling back.

Dealers noted steady speculative buying throughout, with automatic buy stops activated above 108.50 cents basis December. The expiry today of November options lent further strength to futures, dealers said, as traders hedged sales of 110-cent November calls.

Supply jitters resurfaced earlier in the week, when the CSCE reported its gradable stock levels had fallen to their lowest level in 12 years. Since then, the spot December contract has surged 6.85 cents a lb, or six percent.
While origin selling has kept a lid on the gains, dealers said the squeeze on the spot month would persist until more coffee began to flow in from Latin America near the end of 1996.

"Part of it is just a short-term logisitical problem," said one dealer. "Until you actually start to see more production from Central America, supplies are going to be tight. For now, any of the fresh coffee that comes in is quickly bought up."
The nearby switch swelled to 5.65 cents on Friday, from 5.15 the previous day.

A report issued overnight by U.K. trade house calling for a surprisingly large supply deficit in 1996/97 added to the bullish momentum, dealers said. Brokers GNI forecast a world supply shortfall of 4.48 million bags in 1996/97, followed by a 2.76 million bag surplus in 1997/98. Previously, German statistician F.O. Licht had pegged the deficit at around one million bags.
On the charts, December faced a key upside hurdle at 113 cents, followed by 115. Support was noted at 108.50-108, and then 104.50 and 100.00.
-- Wendy Pollack, New York Commodities Desk +1 212 859 1640
